llm.summary: The skill is a real PatentMax patent-search client, but it exposes broader search, analytics, billing, credential, and external-transmission behavior than the inventor-lookup description clearly suggests.

dimensions.detail: Bash, Read, Write, and Glob are broadly useful for this workflow, and external API access is disclosed, but the client sends queries and Authorization headers to a base URL that can be overridden by PATENTMAX_BASE_URL without an allowlist.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package dependency, service setup, or hidden install mechanism was found. The shipped client uses the Python standard library.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main instructions narrow use to inventor lists, while referenced documentation expands into technical prior-art searches, company analysis, external registry checks, and report generation. That mismatch can lead an agent to process and transmit data outside the expected inventor-list workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores a trial API key, budget/session state, candidate ledgers, and patent caches under ~/.patentmax. The trial key path is documented and chmod 0600 is attempted, and no background service or durable system hook was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The top-level skill is framed as inventor patent lookup and CSV export, but the referenced tool guide and Python client also support general patent search, company profiling, full patent retrieval, citations, similar patents, figures, statistics, and broader report workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending inventor names, organizations, patent queries, and any technical search text to PatentMax/ip930.com, and if you accept that the included client can do more than inventor-list export. Avoid setting PATENTMAX_BASE_URL unless you fully trust the destination, and do not use confidential technical details unless external API processing is acceptable.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: The client legitimately sends an API key to PatentMax, but the unvalidated PATENTMAX_BASE_URL override is a real hardening and scoping concern because it can redirect credentials and patent queries if the environment is controlled.
[TP4] unexpected: The mismatch is supported by artifact evidence: the skill advertises inventor lookup, while the referenced documentation and client expose broader patent search, company profiling, citation, similar-patent, and report workflows.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Several documented workflows go beyond inventor lookup, including general patent reports and external verification against registries or non-patent literature. These are not malicious by themselves, but they are under-scoped for this manifest.
[LP1] expected: Outbound access to api.ip930.com is necessary for the stated PatentMax lookup function and is repeatedly disclosed, but the effective network authority is broader because it runs through Bash and the Python client rather than a narrowed permission.
[SQP-2] expected: Local trial-key persistence is disclosed in the FAQ and implemented with restrictive file permissions, so it is expected integration behavior, though users should understand a credential is stored on disk.
[E1] expected: External transmission of inventor names, patent queries, and possibly technical content is core to using a hosted patent database and is disclosed; the concern is mainly user awareness and scope, not evidence of covert exfiltration.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language defaults are visible throughout the artifacts and align with the PatentMax China-focused workflow. This is a usability/localization issue rather than a security issue.
